methodology.heading: Methodology
methodology.p1: The data come from the monthly lists published by the National Health Insurance Fund of Hungary (NEAK): vacant dental and GP services, vacant dental services with terminated contracts, and the registries of contracted providers. NEAK's data are informative in nature and reflect the monthly financing-contract status — they are not real-time operational data.
methodology.p2: A district is “vacant” when it has no contracted physician. This is not the same as “unserved”: residents of vacant districts are covered by a substitute physician. The “terminated contract” category marks dental districts whose financing contract has also ended — NEAK publishes no such list for the GP branch. Long-term vacancy is a legal category: under Government Decree 313/2011 (XII. 23.) it applies to districts where at least 6 months have passed since the contract ended.
methodology.p3: The denominator of the vacancy rate is the number of unique primary-care district codes (FIN or HSZ) in NEAK's registries. On the dental branch adult, paediatric, mixed and school-youth services count (on-call and university services and specialist care do not); on the GP branch, districts with a territorial care obligation (T) — practices without one (TN) are excluded, as they cannot appear on the vacancy list either.
methodology.p4: Practice coordinates are determined with OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service. Where an address could not be identified precisely, the settlement centre is marked and flagged on the map. District boundaries are not officially published, so the map colours at county level and shows districts as points.
methodology.p5: On the GP branch the settlement search is based on the official list of settlements served by each district, so small villages can also be found; the dental registry only records the practice seat, so there the search covers the practices' settlements and the settlements served by terminated districts.
methodology.p6: The full processing code and every month's raw source file are public in the project repository — every number can be traced back to its original source. The contracted physician's name of a filled practice is shown from NEAK's public contracted-provider database; we never publish a personal name for a vacant or terminated district or for a substitute physician.
methodology.p7: The per-capita indicators (share of population living in a vacant district; districts per 10,000 residents; settlement populations) use the resident population of the HCSO Gazetteer as of 1 January 2025. This single edition is applied to every archived month — for historical months this is an approximation, noted here. Settlements are identified by HCSO code and settlement name; Budapest's districts are counted separately.
methodology.p8: The legal category of long-term vacant districts is taken from the continuously updated lists of the OKFŐ Primary Care Directorate (alapellatas.okfo.gov.hu). The list carries no NEAK code, so matching uses the settlement, the service type and the starting month of the vacancy; the list's as-of date is shown in the interface. The flag applies to the current month and is not applied retroactively to historical months.
methodology.embedText: The map can be embedded in any page with the code below (parameter k: dental or gp; optional parameter m: county name):
methodology.p9: The EESZT supplement (source H) is built from three public registers of the EESZT master-data publication: NEAK_FINSZOLG (financed services), EUSZOLG_PUBLIKUS (healthcare providers) and EUSZOLG_ENGEDELY_PUBLIKUS (operating licences). Matching uses official codes only: from the NEAK FIN code through the organisational-unit code to the licence of the district's own profession (GP 6301–6303, dental 1300/1304/1305). We check whether the licensed premises lie in the district's settlement and whether the licensee's tax number matches the financed provider; differences are flagged, and where a FIN points to several licences at different premises no premises are shown. The district number is extracted from the official service name with a strict pattern. The provider name is shown only for filled districts; for vacant districts no free-text name field is taken over, as organisational-unit names often carry the former physician's name. On the EESZT map each district is drawn at its licensed premises; addresses are geocoded with OpenStreetMap Nominatim (at most 1 request per second, cached). Where an address cannot be resolved at street level, the settlement centre is used — shown as a fainter point on the map and in the "approximate location" column; districts without coordinates are not drawn.

why.heading: Why does primary care matter?
why.lead: The GP, the paediatrician and the dentist are the gateway to healthcare: they are the first to see a complaint, they know the family, the medical history, the everyday life of the settlement. Primary care is not “minor medicine” — it is the level where a large share of diseases can be prevented or caught in time.

gp.title: General practitioner
gp.text: Managing chronic diseases — hypertension, diabetes —, organising screenings, vaccinations, and the first examination that decides whether specialist care is needed. Where a district is unfilled, all of this is squeezed into a substitute's reduced consulting hours.

ped.title: Paediatrician
ped.text: Age-linked status examinations, the vaccination schedule and monitoring development are the basis of recognising childhood diseases early. Vacancies in paediatric districts affect the youngest — see them on the map with the “paediatric” type filter.

dental.title: Dentist
dental.text: Caries and periodontal disease are preventable, and early detection of oral cancer can save lives — all of which depends on regular dental screening. In a vacant district the population typically only has local access to emergency care: prevention is the first thing to fall away.

why.chainIntro: Switch between what happens to the same patient with and without a filled district:
why.dataTie: Today {gpPop} people in Hungary live in a vacant GP district and {dentalPop} in a vacant dental district — for them this chain is not a given.
why.disclaimer: The relationships above are general public-health knowledge; we make numerical claims only from our own, sourced data.
chainOkDesc: The district has a doctor: complaints are not left unanswered, examination is available locally.
At regular screening even a still symptomless change comes to light in time.
A disease found early is simpler to treat: medication, care, follow-up.
The complication never happens — the patient lives their life, the hospital never enters the picture.
chainBrokenDesc: The district has no doctor: the practice is closed, substitution is available elsewhere and less often.
Screenings are missed — for those who cannot reach a doctor, nobody looks for anything.
The symptomless change grows quietly and surfaces late, with complaints.
A late diagnosis means more serious intervention and longer, costlier care.
chainOkDentalDesc: The district has a dentist: complaints and the annual check-up are both available locally, in time.
At screening even tiny, symptomless decay comes to light in time.
Decay found early is simple to treat: one small filling and done.
The teeth stay sound — with regular check-ups, major intervention never enters the picture.
chainBrokenDentalDesc: The district has no dentist: the practice is closed, locally only emergency care is available at best.
Screenings are missed — nobody notices the tiny decay.
Decay spreads quietly and announces itself with pain and swelling.
A tooth beyond saving must be extracted — replacement is longer, more painful and far more expensive.

eesztInfo.title: How we matched the EESZT data
eesztInfo.subtitle: EESZT download: {asOf} · NEAK data: {month} · every step is traceable
eesztInfo.p1: The map is built on NEAK's monthly vacancy lists and contracted-provider registry; these define the districts and their FIN codes. The EESZT supplement adds no districts. It only attaches further official public data to existing districts: the district number, the licensed premises, on-call participation, public funding, and for filled districts the financed provider. Whatever cannot be linked unambiguously is not shown, and we give the reason.
eesztInfo.regFinszolg: Services financed by NEAK: FIN code (FINKOD), organisational-unit code (NNGYK9_KOD), service type (TIP), official service name (FINNEV), provider name (INEV), institution code (INTKOD) and the first 8 digits of the provider's tax number (ADOIGSZ_8).
eesztInfo.regEuszolg: Register of healthcare providers: provider id (EUSZOLG_AZONOSITO), name, tax number, seat.
eesztInfo.regEngedely: Operating licences: licence id, organisational-unit code (SZERVEZETI_EGYSEG_KOD), provider id, premises address, profession (SZAKMA_KOD), public funding (KOZFINANSZIROZOTT) and on-call participation.
eesztInfo.p2: The link in the first column opens the register on the public EESZT portal. The raw download is archived unchanged in the project repository, so it can be re-run and checked at any time.
eesztInfo.p3a: The EESZT master-data page loads its data from a public REST endpoint. We used the same endpoint, paging with 500 rows per page:
eesztInfo.p3b: Each download checks that the number of rows received exactly matches the total the server reports (totalRowCount), that there are no duplicate rows, and that the total did not change during the download. If any check fails, the download stops with an error and no data is taken over. The download code:
eesztInfo.s1: Starting point: every district in NEAK's latest monthly data (filled, vacant, terminated) with its FIN code.
eesztInfo.s2: FIN code → NEAK_FINSZOLG: looked up in the FINKOD field. Only rows of the branch's own type are used: TIP = FOG for dental, TIP = HSZ for GP. A FIN code can appear in several rows (several organisational units); all of them are kept.
eesztInfo.s3: NEAK_FINSZOLG.NNGYK9_KOD → EUSZOLG_ENGEDELY_PUBLIKUS.SZERVEZETI_EGYSEG_KOD: the unit's operating licences are found by exact match on the unit code.
eesztInfo.s4: Profession filter: only licences for the district's own profession are accepted. GP: 6301 general practice, 6302 paediatric general practice, 6303 mixed general practice. Dental: 1300 dental care, 1304 paediatric dentistry, 1305 school dentistry.
eesztInfo.s5: Choosing the licence: if there are several, we take the one whose premises lie in the district's NEAK settlement and that names an actual address.
eesztInfo.s6: Provider check: the licence's EUSZOLG_AZONOSITO leads to the provider in EUSZOLG_PUBLIKUS, whose tax number (first 8 digits) is compared with NEAK_FINSZOLG.ADOIGSZ_8.
eesztInfo.p4: Every link rests on an exact match of official codes. No name-based or similarity (fuzzy) matching is used anywhere. The matching code:
eesztInfo.c1: if a FIN code belongs to several organisational units whose licences name different addresses, we do not pick one: no premises are shown for that district, and it appears among the unmatched with the reason "ambiguous".
eesztInfo.c2: if the licensed premises lie in another settlement than the district's NEAK seat, the premises are shown but flagged ("differs from the district's NEAK seat"). "Budapest" and "Budapest VIII. kerület" are treated as matching.
eesztInfo.c3: whether the licensee's and the financed provider's tax numbers match is shown in its own column ("Tax number matches").
eesztInfo.c4: the district number and provider name are shown only when every row of a FIN code carries the same value.
eesztInfo.c5: every district falls into exactly one category: it either has a matched licence or a recorded reason why not. The build stops if matched plus unmatched districts do not add up to the total.
eesztInfo.n1: The financed provider name and institution code are shown only for filled districts (the contracted provider NEAK itself publishes).
eesztInfo.n2: For vacant and terminated districts no free-text name field is taken over: organisational-unit names often carry the former physician's name ({n} such vacant districts in the current data; their names are not published).
eesztInfo.n3: Of the trace codes, the provider id is also given only for filled districts; the other codes (organisational unit, licence) carry no personal data.
eesztInfo.n4: The build checks these rules automatically and stops on any violation; tests protect them as well.
eesztInfo.p7: The official service name (FINNEV) is free text, so we extract only the district number, with a strict pattern. For example "Tatabánya 8. sz. gyermek körzet." → "8. gyermek körzet", "BETÖLTETLEN - 1. körzet, Beremend" → "1. körzet". If the pattern is not unambiguous, or the result contains a personal-name marker, no district number is shown.
eesztInfo.p8: Licensed premises addresses are geocoded with OpenStreetMap Nominatim, at most 1 request per second, cached. We first search at street level with the postcode, then without it. If neither returns a result, the settlement centre is used, shown as a fainter point on the map and in the "Approximate location" column. Districts without coordinates are not drawn. The geocoding code:
eesztInfo.p9: Percentages refer to the total number of districts. The list of unmatched districts, with reasons, is available in the table marked with the warning icon, filterable and exportable.
eesztInfo.h10: Worked example: one district's full path
eesztInfo.p10: The Sásd dental district (vacant), step by step. Each link opens, on the public EESZT portal, exactly the row the data was taken from.
eesztInfo.e1: NEAK FIN code: {fin}. In NEAK_FINSZOLG it has one row of type FOG.
eesztInfo.e2: In that row the organisational-unit code (NNGYK9_KOD) is {unit}.
eesztInfo.e3: The unit's dental operating licence: {licence}; premises: {address}; profession: {profession}.
eesztInfo.e4: Check: premises in the district's settlement: {settlement}; licensee's tax number matches the financed provider: {provider}.
eesztInfo.e5: Because the district is vacant, no provider name or provider id is published; the premises, on-call duty and public funding are shown.
eesztInfo.h11: How can you verify it yourself?
eesztInfo.v1: Click any point on the map: the "Trace" part of the side panel links to the EESZT portal — FIN code, organisational unit, licence, and for filled districts the provider.
eesztInfo.v2: In the full table, the "Organisational unit code", "Licence id" and "Provider id" columns can be switched on from the "Columns" menu; they link to EESZT too.
eesztInfo.v3: The filtered table can be exported as CSV or TSV and compared with the source in bulk.
eesztInfo.v4: The raw download, the download code and the matching code are public in the project repository; running them on the same download gives the same result.
eesztInfo.l1: EESZT data reflects the day of download, NEAK data the month; the two may differ (e.g. a freshly filled district).
eesztInfo.l2: The licensed premises are not necessarily the actual consulting place, and one licence may cover several districts (see the "Shared organisational unit" column).
eesztInfo.l3: The district number appears only where the official name contains it unambiguously.
eesztInfo.l4: Points at a settlement centre indicate an approximate location only.

svc.s1: From the NEAK contracted dental provider list we take the {what}. District services are not included here — the other tab describes those.
svc.s2: The service's unit code is looked up in the EESZT financed-services register (NEAK_FINSZOLG), filtered to the FOG (dental) service type.
svc.s3: From that row we read the organisational unit's NNGYK9 code and use it to find the operating licences in the licence register (EUSZOLG_ENGEDELY_PUBLIKUS).
svc.s4: Of those licences we accept only the one issued for the service's own profession ({professions}).
svc.s5: From the licence we take the premises, the profession code, the public funding flag and the on-call participation; the provider's tax number is cross-checked against the financing register.
svc.s6: If the code points at several units whose licences disagree on the premises, we pick none: the service goes on the “unmatched” list with its reason.
svc.c1: A licence counts only with the profession code that belongs to the service type ({professions}). A licence for something else does not prove the service operates there.
svc.c2t: No pick when it is ambiguous
svc.c2: With several units and several different premises we assign none, and show what the candidates were instead.
svc.c3t: A licence that names its premises wins
svc.c3: Among candidate licences we take the one that names its premises and sits in the settlement NEAK gives.
svc.c4: The licensee's tax number is compared with the financing register's; the result is a column of its own and never changes the match.
svc.n1: NEAK itself publishes the physicians in the contracted-provider list, so they are shown — for on-call services the whole roster, as the list gives it.
svc.n2: The provider name, NEAK code and EESZT provider id are carried only where the list also names a contracted physician; {n} services name none, and there these fields stay empty.
svc.n3: The build checks this automatically and stops on a violation; tests guard it too.
svc.p7: A specialist unit code is not a FIN code: it can contain a letter (02006A425, for example), so a 9-character alphanumeric code is expected — nothing is dropped silently. For on-call services the list gives one row per physician, so one code has many rows; they are merged into one service and the row count is kept.
svc.p8: The map location is the EESZT licensed premises where there is a match, and the NEAK surgery address otherwise. The table's “source of the map location” column always says which. Geocoding is the same cached Nominatim process:
svc.p9: The highlighted numbers open the affected services as a filterable, exportable table; for the ambiguous cases every candidate licence is listed row by row.
svc.p10: The full path of a real service ({type}), from the current data:
svc.e1: In the NEAK list, the {type} service with code {code} ({settlement}).
svc.e2: In the financing register it belongs to organisational unit {unit}.
svc.e3: That unit's licence for the profession: {licence} — {profession}, premises: {address}.
svc.e4: Does the premises settlement match NEAK's: {settlementMatch}. Does the provider tax number match: {providerMatch}.
svc.v1: Every code is a link: clicking it in the table opens exactly that row on the public EESZT portal.
svc.v2: The raw EESZT files and the NEAK provider list are both in the repository, with their dates — any number can be recomputed.
svc.v3: The ETL recomputes every number from the raw files; if the row counts disagree, or a service is neither matched nor explained, the build fails.
svc.l1: These services are not districts: they count towards neither the district total nor the vacancy rate.
svc.l2: The NEAK list is indicative and lags changes made during the month.
svc.l3: The licence register shows the operating licence, not opening hours: a licence does not mean the {what} are available right now.

xc.s1: We take the NEAK records the code chain could not pair with an EESZT licence — districts and services alike.
xc.s2: The NEAK surgery address is normalized (accents folded, abbreviations expanded: u. → utca, krt → körút, house number extracted, Budapest districts unified), and every premises address in the EESZT licence register is normalized the same way.
xc.s3: We check whether the NEAK address holds an EESZT licence in the record's own profession family (dental 13xx, GP 63xx). If it does, we check whether that licence sits under the record's own organisational unit or a different one.
xc.s4: With no hit at the address we look for weaker evidence: the same street at another house number, then — where NEAK also names a provider — a provider-name match against the EESZT provider register (words of 3+ characters, from 50% overlap).
xc.s5: The other direction is checked too: which dental and GP services appear in the EESZT financed-services register while the published NEAK lists do not contain them.
xc.c1t: A suggestion is not a pairing
xc.c1: Nothing from the cross-check enters the district data: it never changes a match and never counts towards the coverage numbers. It is a separate table with its own reasoning.
xc.c2: A dental district only matches a dental licence (13xx), a GP district a GP one (63xx). If the address holds only another profession's licence, that is reported as its own result.
xc.c3: A column states whether the hit came from the premises address, the street name or the provider name, and a full sentence explains it.
xc.c4t: The name policy holds here too
xc.c4: Free-text names appear only where NEAK itself publishes a contracted physician; everywhere else the output carries codes, addresses and profession names only.
xc.names: The cross-check follows the same name rules as the rest: the free-text names of organisational units and premises are never exported, because they often carry a physician's name. The suggestions rest on codes, addresses and profession names.
xc.rEesztOnly: Services that exist in EESZT only
xc.p9: Clicking a number lists every candidate row by row (unit, licence id, premises, profession), filterable and exportable.
xc.l1: An address match is not proof: several services can share a building, and a mistyped address can produce an accidental hit.
xc.l2: A provider-name match is the weakest evidence: a rename or a similarly named company can mislead.
xc.l3: The “in EESZT only” list is not necessarily a missing district: it can be an on-call, school or other service the published NEAK lists do not carry.

extra.oncallExplain: Contracted dental on-call services on the primary-care level. The NEAK list names every physician on the duty roster on its own row, so one service has several registry rows. These are not districts and never enter the vacancy rate.
extra.universityExplain: Dental primary care run by the university clinics. They carry no territorial obligation, so they stay out of the district denominator.
extra.specialistExplain: Every contracted dental specialist service: oral surgery, orthodontics, radiology, periodontology, paediatric and university specialist care, and care for people with disabilities. The join is the one used above, with the EESZT profession code that belongs to the service type (radiology → 1306, for example).

why.noUnitLicence: The service's organisational unit ({units}) holds no licence for its own profession in the EESZT licence register.

crosscheck.explain: Where the code chain (FIN → organisational unit → licence) found nothing, we look from the other side: is the same surgery or the same provider in EESZT after all — possibly under a different organisational unit? Addresses and names are compared in normalized form (accents, abbreviations, house number), and every row states what the hit is based on. These are suggestions, not official pairings.

crosscheck.note: The comparison runs between the NEAK contracted-provider list, the EESZT financed-services register, the provider register and the licence register, as of {asOf}.

verdict.otherProfessionAtAddress: Only another profession at the address

why.otherUnit: At the surgery address NEAK gives, EESZT holds a {profession} licence ({place}) — but under organisational unit {unit}, not the record's own ({own}). Most likely the same surgery, filed under a different unit.
why.ownUnit: At this address the record's own unit ({unit}) does hold a {profession} licence; the automatic join rejected it because of “{reason}” — worth checking by hand.
why.otherProfession: There is an EESZT licence at the address, but for another profession ({professions}); no {kind} licence was found there.
why.street: The same street has a {profession} licence ({place}) at a different house number — a spelling difference or the neighbouring building.
why.provider: The provider name matches an EESZT provider by {overlap}, and that provider holds a {profession} licence in the settlement ({unit}) — but the addresses differ.
why.noneInSettlement: The settlement has {n} same-profession EESZT licences, none of them at the NEAK address or street; the provider name gave no hit either.
why.noneAtAll: The settlement has no same-profession EESZT licence at all — the surgery cannot be identified by address or by name.
